title: Hydrogen storage by carbon nanotube and their films under ambient pressure
material_description: sample 1 | arc-discharge CNT powder (169.5 mg) containing MWNTs of about 60 wt%, 0.5-2 um in length and 10-25 nm in diameter; the rest carbon nanoparticles and amorphous carbon
source_location: main-2.png (p. 498), Section 3 'Results and conclusion', paragraph 1 (text); run shown in Fig. 2 (main-3.png, p. 499)
notes: Printed: 'At pressure just greater than 1 atm, the H2 storage experiment with sample 1 ... nearly reached an equilibrium value 35 h later. The calculated H2 storage capacity for sample 1 is 0.26 wt%.' Pressure not printed as a number ('just greater than 1 atm'), so pressure_unstated = true; Fig. 2 (pressure versus time, not an isotherm) is not digitized. Separate run from the 0.52 atm experiment (separate figure; paper attributes a pressure rise in that run to H2 remaining from 'the last time'), so own isotherm_id with one value. Temperature printed only as 'room temperature'. Method: closed-cell manometric method; H2 (99.99%) sealed in a brass sample cell of 49.30 ml and uptake calculated from the pressure decrease measured by a MEMS vacuum sensor (10^2 to 10^6 Pa, accuracy 20 Pa); coded volumetric_sieverts. Instrument: the authors' own apparatus ('our system', schematic in Fig. 1, brass cell, MEMS sensor), coded instrument_identified = true. Identical runs on the empty cell were used to correct for the effect of the cell wall; no determination of the free (gas) volume with the sample present is described, so calibration_described = false. Degassing printed: sample heated to 353 K in the cell, then vacuum-degassed for 4-5 h (to 3.7 x 10^-5 tau); degas_temperature_c converted from 353 K; tau read as Torr (3.7e-5 Torr = 0.004932914 Pa); duration printed as a range 4-5 h and not stored. Basis not named in the paper; basis_inferred excess by the volumetric instrumental default. No surface area or pore volume is reported for any sample. measuring_lab_id: corresponding author printed 'Zhu Changchun*' and 'Z. Changchun' in the footnote; surname taken as printed by the paper ('Changchun'), although the e-mail chzhu@xjtu.edu.cn suggests Zhu is the family name.
